newsitem.title: USA: Petro says heat oil prices may have peaked.
newsitem.headline: Petro says heat oil prices may have peaked.

text.p: Petroleum Heat & Power Inc chief executive Irik Sevin said heating oil prices may have peaked on the wholesale and retail level after surging in the past several months.
"Off the cuff, I tend to think that it has peaked," said Sevin, who is also president of one of the largest retail heating oil distributors in the U.S. Northeast.
But, he emphasized he could not guarantee such a prediction since heating oil prices are subject to the vagrancies of the weather and world politics.
Sevin made his statements on a conference call with analysts and reporters following the release of Petro's third quarter results.
Earlier Thursday, Petro said its third quarter loss narrowed to $1.63 per share from a loss of $1.65 per share a year ago.

The company typically reports a loss in the third quarter since it reflects the summer months. The First Call consensus analysts' earnings estimate is 0.20 per share for 1996, but Sevin declined comment on earnings projections.

In some regions in the Northeast, heating oil is retailing for 20 cents more per gallon after historically low supplies sent heating oil futures to post-Gulf War highs on the New York Mercantile Exchange.
The price of heating oil had risen to the high of 76.75 cents a gallon in October from 49.20 cents in June.
Heating oil futures prices have since come down after oil refiners began to replenish low supplies.
"I felt that 75 cents was not a sustainable level for heating oil ...," said Sevin.
"Self-corrective measures (by the market), such as refiners producing more stuff, were part of a flux of characteristics that brought the prices down," said Sevin.
